Source: modules/admin/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/admin/README.md)

# admin (#335)

The app's back office. It provides:
- a layout with the `admin.sidebar` slot;
- a dashboard with the `admin.dashboard` slot, which the installed modules fill;
- the users page, where the admin role is granted and revoked;
- the audit viewer.

## Install

```sh
bunx renox add admin          # needs auth, i18n and audit
```

```toml
admin = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/admin", config = { title = "Back office" } }
```

The app grants the first admin with `ctx.authz.roles.assign(user_id, "admin")` from its own code, for example a one-off setup route. After that, admins grant each other from the users page.

## Pages

| Page | Needs | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<mount>` | `admin.access` | The user count, the latest audit events (with `audit.read`), and the cards of `admin.dashboard` |
| `<mount>/users?q=` | `admin.access` | The users from auth's public view and whether each holds the admin role |
| Grant and revoke buttons on the users page | `admin.users` (sensitive) | Shown under `r-can`. An admin cannot revoke their own role |
| `<mount>/audit?actor=&action=` | `admin.access` | The audit module's trail. It also needs `audit.read`, the auditor role; without it the page says so and shows no rows |

The default policy grants both admin actions to the `admin` role.

## Slots other modules fill

| Module | `admin.sidebar` link | Shown when the user holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| billing | All invoices | `billing.manage` |
| storage | Files | `storage.manage` |
| jobs | Jobs | `jobs.read` |
| notifications | Notification preferences | (everyone) |

A filler renders only when its module is installed and the user holds its `requires` action.

## Not built

- **CRUD scaffolding from `[admin.tables]`.** A module may read and write only its own `<name>__*` tables (the authorizer, `ops.md` section 3), so a back office module cannot edit the app's `app__*` tables. Scaffolding needs a contract change: either an app-granted table permission for one module, or a scaffold that `renox` generates into the app's own pages.
- **The organisations page.**
- **Settings beyond `admin__settings`.**

## Tests

With `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`, `tests/app.test.ts` runs in an app with auth, audit and jobs on the worker:
- the back office is refused without `admin.access`;
- the sidebar renders jobs' link and not billing's, which is not installed;
- the admin role is granted and revoked, but not an admin's own;
- the audit viewer is refused without the auditor role and shows the role decisions to an auditor;
- the users table header is snapshotted in `ltr` and `rtl`.

---

Source: modules/audit/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/audit/README.md)

# audit

An append-only audit trail for an app and its modules (`docs/18-build-plan.md` M8; `docs/11-authorization.md` "Cross-module context and audit"). Modules and the app record events through one service. Nothing can edit or delete them. The platform's authorization decisions on sensitive actions appear in the same trail.

## Install

```toml
[modules]
audit = { version = "^1.0", config = { retain_days = 365 } }
```

A module that records events adds `audit = "^1.0"` to its `[dependencies]` and `services = ["audit.record"]` to its `[imports]`. Depending on `audit` also lets that module read the platform view `renox__authz_audit_v1` directly.

## The event

`audit__events`, one row per event:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Random, sortable by time |
| `at` | Unix ms (as in `renox__authz_audit`) |
| `actor_kind` | `user`, `agent` or `system` |
| `actor_id` | The user id (the agent's user for `agent`), or `system:<module>` |
| `client` | The agent's client name (`agent` only) |
| `action` | `<module>.<verb>`, such as `invoice.refund` or `auth.login` |
| `resource_type`, `resource_id` | What was acted on (`billing:Invoice`, `inv_1`), optional |
| `result` | `ok`, `denied` or `failed` |
| `details` | A JSON object, redacted (below), at most 16 KB |
| `request_id` | Optional, to tie a row to logs |
| `source` | `record`, or the name of the event a listener recorded |

### Actor kinds

- `user`: a person, acting in a browser.
- `agent`: a person's agent through the app's `/mcp`, with the agent's client name in `client`. It can do only what its user can (`docs/20-ai-agents-mcp.md` section 5, "Attribution").
- `system`: the platform or a module acting on its own (an event handler, a job), as `system:<module>`.

### Redaction

The redaction rule applies to `details` at any depth. Each key is split into words (`apiKey`, `api_key` and `API-KEY` all become `api key`). The key's value becomes `"[redacted]"` when either:

- one of the words is `password`, `pass`, `secret`, `token`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `credential`, `otp`, `pin`, `cvv`, `iban`, `signature`, `salt`, `hash` (and a few spellings of these); or
- the words run together into `apikey`, `privatekey`, `accesskey`, `cardnumber`, `sessionid` or `clientsecret`.

Values are never inspected, so a secret stored under an innocent key stays: name keys for what they hold.

## Services

| Service | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `record(event)` | `{ id }`. `event` is `{ action, actor: { kind, id, client? }, resource?: { type, id? }, result?, details?, request_id? }`. A malformed event throws |
| `query(filter?)` | `{ events, next }`, newest first. The events are this module's rows merged with the platform's decisions from `renox__authz_audit_v1` (`kind: "authz"`, `result` `allow`/`deny`). Filter: `actor`, `action` (or a prefix ending in `.`), `since`, `until`, `platform` (default `true`), `limit` (1 to 200, default 50), `cursor` (the previous page's `next`). Requires `audit.read` |
| `exportEvents(filter?, purpose?)` | Runs the hook `audit.export` once per page of 200 (`{ events, page, last, purpose }`); returns `{ events, pages }`. For F7's reports and the F6 erasure task (#120). Requires `audit.read` |
| `prune()` | Deletes rows older than `retain_days`, never fewer than 30 days; returns `{ deleted }`. The module's job `jobs/prune.ts` runs it every night at 02:30 UTC (#297), so the app no longer has to; the app may still call it |

## Who may read

`audit.read` is the module's action, and it is `sensitive`: every read, allowed or denied, writes its own row in `renox__authz_audit`. `policies/audit.cedar` allows it to the role `auditor`. The app grants that role (`ctx.authz.roles.assign(userId, "auditor")`); the module never grants it.

## Listeners

These events become rows with no code in the app (`hooks.ts`, `on`):

| Event | Actor |
| --- | --- |
| `auth.login`, `auth.password_changed`, `auth.agent_token_revoked` | The user |
| `authz.roles_changed` | `system:authz`; `details` names the user, the role and `op` |
| `org.created`, `org.member_added` | The user |
| `org.member_removed` | `by`, the user who removed the member |

## Append-only

- **Updates are refused.** `audit__events` has triggers that `RAISE(ABORT)` on every `UPDATE`.
- **Young rows cannot be deleted.** The same triggers refuse a `DELETE` of any row younger than 30 days.
- **This covers every connection.** It holds for the module's own code, other modules, the app, and a tool that opens the file.
- **Other modules cannot write the table at all.** The SQLite authorizer refuses them `audit__*`.
- **The platform table is the authorizer's job.** `renox__authz_audit` (#277) is refused `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `DROP` and `ALTER` for everyone.

The manifest has no `append_only` permission (#272 did not add one), so the triggers are the module's rule. To make them possible, the migration runner lets a module create triggers on its own tables. Their bodies may only `select raise(...)`, with no subquery.

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retain_days` | 365 | `prune` deletes rows older than this, from 30 to 3650 days |

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs `tests/audit.test.ts` against `tests/app`. That app has auth, org, audit, and the fixture `tamper`: a module that depends on audit, tries to edit its rows, and fills `audit.export`. The tests cover:

- the redaction rule;
- the listeners;
- `record` from another module;
- append-only, against module code, app code and the file itself (the `docs/24-threat-model.md` row "Audit library append-only; tenant cannot edit or delete audit rows");
- `query` refused without the role and allowed with it, with the platform decisions joined and paged;
- export;
- prune.

The policy cases are in `policies/tests/audit.json`.

---

Source: modules/auth/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/auth/README.md)

# auth

Users, passwords, sessions, and the sign-in pages for a Renox app, as a module (`docs/10-modules.md`; M1 of `docs/18-build-plan.md`). An app that installs it has accounts with no auth code of its own: `examples/shop` is the reference (#241).

## Install

```sh
renox add i18n          # auth's pages take their locale from i18n (#244)
renox add auth          # shows the tables, hosts, secrets and slot it asks for; approve with y
renox migrate           # creates auth__* (renox dev does it on start)
```

`renox.toml`:

```toml
[modules]
auth = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/auth", config = { session_idle_hours = 24 } }
```

The pages are under the mount: `/auth/login`, `/auth/register`, `/auth/account`, `/auth/magic`, `/auth/reset`, and the OAuth routes `/auth/oauth/<provider>/{start,callback}`.

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session_idle_hours` | 24 | A session ends after this many hours without a request |
| `session_absolute_days` | 30 | A session ends this many days after sign-in, used or not; the cookie's `Max-Age` |
| `password_min_length` | 12 | At register, password change, and reset |
| `login_path` | `/auth/login` | Where `requireUser` and `loginUrl` send a signed-out visitor; change it with the mount |
| `google_client_id`, `github_client_id`, `microsoft_client_id` | `""` | OAuth client ids; a provider is on when its id and its secret are set |

## Permissions

| What | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tables | `auth__*` | users, sessions, identities, tokens, attempts |
| Network | `accounts.google.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com`, `www.googleapis.com`, `github.com`, `api.github.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `graph.microsoft.com` | OAuth token endpoints, OIDC signing keys, the GitHub API; nothing else |
| Secrets | `AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | Only for the providers you set up |
| Slots | `app.header` | The user menu |

Other modules read users through the view `auth__public_users_v1` (`id`, `email`, `display_name`, `created_at`), never the tables: the authorizer refuses `auth__users` to them.

## Services

Through `import { auth } from "renox:modules"` (or `ctx.services.auth`):

| Service | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `currentUser()` | The signed-in user of this request, or `null` |
| `currentSession()` | `{ id, user }` of the live session, or `null`. `id` is not the cookie token: other modules key per-session state by it (org's active organisation) |
| `requireUser()` | The user, or throws `AuthRequiredError` (`code: "AUTH_REQUIRED"`, `status: 401`; through the broker, `RENOX_MODULE_SERVICE`) |
| `loginUrl(next?)` | `/auth/login?next=…`; `next` kept only when it is a path of the app |
| `register({ email, password, display_name? })` | `{ message }` (a confirmation link is mailed; the same message when the email already has an account, which gets a mail saying so) or `{ error }` for a bad email or password |
| `login({ email, password })` | `{ user, cookie }` or `{ error }`: the same error for an unknown email, a wrong password, and a locked account |
| `logout()` | `{ cookie }` (clears it); the session is revoked server side |
| `sendMagicLink({ email })`, `requestPasswordReset({ email })` | `{ message }`: the same in every case |
| `confirmPasswordReset({ token, password })` | `{ cookie }` or `{ error }` |
| `principal(sessionId)` | `{ id, attrs }` of the signed-in user, or `null` (below, "The principal") |
| `resumeLogin(ticket)` | `{ cookie, session_id, user_id, next }` for a `resume` ticket of `auth.after_login`, or `null` (unknown, used, or past 10 minutes). Starts the session; the hook does not run again |
| `verifyAgentToken(token)` | `{ principal, scopes, client: { name } }` for a live agent token, or `null`. The cell calls it for `/mcp` |
| `oauthMetadata(issuer)` | The RFC 8414 document the cell serves at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server<mount>/oauth` |
| `listAgentTokens()`, `revokeAgentToken(id)` | The signed-in user's connected agents; revoke one of them |

A page that needs a user:

```ts
import { auth } from "renox:modules";
import { redirect } from "renox";

export async function load(ctx) {
  const user = await auth.currentUser();
  if (user === null) return redirect.safe(await auth.loginUrl(ctx.url.pathname));
  return { auth_user: user };
}
```

## Events

| Event | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `auth.user_registered` | `{ user_id, at, source: "password" \| "oauth" }` |
| `auth.login` | `{ user_id, at }` |
| `auth.password_changed` | `{ user_id, at }` (a reset) |
| `auth.logout` | `{ user_id, at }`: the cell drops the principal from its cache |
| `auth.agent_token_revoked` | `{ token_hash, user_id, at }`: the cell drops the token from its `/mcp` cache |

All durable: written in the transaction of the request, delivered after it commits.

## Hooks

| Hook | When | A filler may |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.before_register` | Before a user is created (`{ email, display_name }`) | Halt with its own response: invite-only, a domain allowlist |
| `auth.after_login` | After the password, magic link, OAuth, phone or passkey check, before any session starts (`{ user_id, next?, resume }`) | Halt with its own response, so no session starts. To resume later, keep `resume` (a single-use ticket, valid 10 minutes) and call `auth.resumeLogin(resume)`, which starts the session. 2fa does this |
| `auth.principal` | Once per request, while the cell resolves the principal (`{ principal: { id, attrs } }`) | Extend `principal.attrs` in place: 2fa sets `mfa_verified`, org sets `org`. Keys outside the platform's user attributes are dropped |
| `auth.send_otp` | A one-time code must reach a phone (`{ to, code, purpose: "login" \| "verify" }`) | Deliver it. whatsapp fills it (#290); an SMS module will in F7. Never log the code |
| `auth.send_sms` | Declared for F7 (`{ to, text }`) | Nothing fills it yet |
| `auth.agent_audit` | An agent was connected or disconnected (`{ action: "connect" \| "revoke", user_id, client_name, scopes, at }`) | Write an audit row (the `audit` library, #288). Never carries the token |
| `auth.send_mail` | A mail must go out (`{ to, template: "magic_link" \| "password_reset" \| "verify_email" \| "account_exists", args: { url, expires_minutes, display_name } }`) | Send it. auth sends no mail itself until the email module (F7). Fill it from a small module of the app (`modules/mailer`, `permissions.hooks = ["auth.send_mail"]`) |

## Slots

`partials/user-menu.html` fills `app.header` when the app's layout has `<r-slot name="app.header" />`. It shows `auth_user.display_name` with a link to the account page, or "Sign in". A page puts `auth_user: await auth.currentUser()` in its data.

## Overrides

Override a template, never the code: put a copy at `overrides/auth/pages/login.html` (or any `pages/` or `partials/` file) in the app. `renox build` compiles it in place of the original and records the original's hash in the app's `overrides.json`. After `renox add auth` brings a new version whose original changed, `renox build` and `renox check` warn with a diff (`--strict` fails). Update the override, then delete its entry from `overrides.json`.

## Sessions and cookies

- `__Host-renox_auth=<32 random bytes, hex>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=<absolute expiry>`. Only the token's SHA-256 is stored.
- A new session at every sign-in; the browser's previous one is revoked (fixation). A password change revokes every other session and rotates this one.
- This is not the platform's page `session.id` (`ops.md` section 14). That one exists before sign-in, lives as long as the browser keeps it, and carries the CSRF token. A user session has its own lifetime and ends at logout.
- Passwords are argon2id at m = 64 MiB, t = 3, p = 1 through `ctx.password` (a platform op, off the isolate thread). An unknown email is checked against a fixed hash, so it costs the same.
- Failure buckets: 10 per account and 30 per IP address per 15 minutes; past either, the same generic message. Magic and reset links: 5 per email per 15 minutes, single use, 15 minutes, bound to the user agent family that asked.
- OAuth: `state` in a 10-minute `__Host-renox_oauth` cookie, compared in constant time; PKCE S256 for Google and Microsoft; ID tokens verified (RS256 against the provider's keys, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce). An existing account is linked only when the provider verified the email.

## The principal

The cell asks `auth.principal` once per request, before any guard (`ops.md` 1.5.0 section 17). Signed out, the answer is `null`, the anonymous principal. Signed in, it is:

```json
{ "id": "<user id>", "attrs": { "email_verified": true, "phone_verified": false, "created_at": 1793310868, "org": "o_1", "mfa_verified": true } }
```

- `email_verified`, `phone_verified` and `created_at` come from auth itself.
- Fillers of the hook `auth.principal` add the rest: `org` from org, `mfa_verified` from 2fa (#287). Only the platform's user attributes are kept (`created_at`, `email_verified`, `mfa_verified`, `org`, `phone_verified`).
- The cell adds the user's role assignments as `roles`.
- The cell caches the principal and drops it on `auth.login`, `auth.logout` and `authz.roles_changed`.
- Code reads it as `ctx.principal`; policies read it as `principal`.

## Sign-in methods

The login page offers the password form and, each behind its own switch:

- a link to phone sign-in (config `phone_login`);
- a link to passkey sign-in (config `passkeys`);
- a button per OAuth provider that has a client id and a secret: Google, GitHub, Microsoft, UAE PASS.

The `2fa` module (#287) fills both `auth.after_login` and `auth.principal`. After any of these methods, it halts the sign-in until the second factor. It keeps the `resume` ticket auth hands to `auth.after_login` fillers and redeems it with `resumeLogin` once the factor passed. It also sets `mfa_verified` on the principal.

Every method ends the same way as the password flow. The hook `auth.after_login` runs first; a filler may halt, and then no session starts (2fa). After it come a new session, `auth.login`, and a 303 to `next`.

### Phone (`phone_login = true`)

- **Pages.** `<mount>/phone` asks for the number and sends a code; `<mount>/phone/verify` takes the code. The account page adds or changes the phone with a code to the new number. A phone signs in only once it is verified.
- **Numbers.** UAE numbers are accepted as `+971 5x xxx xxxx`, `05x xxx xxxx` or `00971…`; numbers in any other E.164 form are accepted too.
- **Codes.** A code is 6 digits, lasts 5 minutes, allows 5 attempts and works once. It is stored as argon2id.
- **Same answer.** The sign-in request answers the same whether or not a user has the number, and sends nothing for an unknown one.
- **Buckets.** At most 5 codes per number and 30 per IP address in 15 minutes.
- **Delivery.** Codes go out through the hook `auth.send_otp`. Install `whatsapp` (#290), which fills it. auth cannot call an optional module, and a hook needs no dependency.

### Passkeys (`passkeys = true`)

- **Adding one.** `<mount>/passkeys/register` (linked from the account page) creates a discoverable credential, ES256 or RS256.
- **Signing in.** `<mount>/passkeys/login` signs in with it, without a username.
- **Verification.** Done with the SDK's `verifyRegistration` and `verifyAssertion`. Challenges are single use and last 5 minutes. The signature counter must grow, so a cloned authenticator is refused.
- **Relying party.** It is the request's host, or config `passkey_rp_id` and `passkey_origin`.
- **Not a second factor.** A passkey here is a way to sign in. A passkey as a second factor is the 2fa module's (#287), in its own table: a user may have either, or both.

### UAE PASS

UAE PASS is an OAuth 2 provider with the user-info endpoint. It is set up with config `uaepass_client_id`, `uaepass_env` (`staging` by default, or `production`) and the secret `AUTH_UAEPASS_CLIENT_SECRET`.

- `uuid` becomes `auth__users.uaepass_uuid`.
- An SOP3 account, a verified identity, sets `verified_identity`.
- The email of SOP2 and SOP3 accounts counts as verified, so it may link an existing account. An SOP1 email does not.

**Production onboarding (owner steps):**

1. Apply for UAE PASS integration as a private-sector service provider through UAE PASS's partner onboarding. Provide the legal entity, the trade licence and the use case.
2. Sign the service provider agreement and complete the security questionnaire.
3. Receive staging credentials. Register `https://<host><mount>/oauth/uaepass/callback` as the redirect URI.
4. Test on staging (`uaepass_env = "staging"`) with UAE PASS staging test accounts. The integration review checks the button design guidelines and the login flow.
5. Request production credentials. Set `uaepass_client_id`, the secret, and `uaepass_env = "production"`.

The requirements for private providers are an open question in `docs/15-roadmap.md`. Check them with the UAE PASS team before you promise the method to a customer.

## Agents (App MCP)

auth is the OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app's `/mcp` (`docs/20-ai-agents-mcp.md` section 2). An agent connects as a user and can do only what the user can.

- Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` names `https://<host><mount>/oauth`. The cell serves its metadata (RFC 8414) from `oauthMetadata`.
- Registration: `POST <mount>/oauth/register` (RFC 7591). Public clients only (`token_endpoint_auth_method: "none"`). Redirect URIs must be `https`, or `http` on loopback.
- Authorization: `GET <mount>/oauth/authorize`. PKCE S256 is required. A signed-out user goes to the login page first.
- Consent: `<mount>/oauth/consent` lists the client, the user, where it returns, and each scope (`tools:*` or `tools:<name>`), with Allow and Deny. It runs no script of its own and cannot be framed.
- Codes: one minute, single use, stored hashed. A failed exchange also burns the code.
- Token: `POST <mount>/oauth/token` returns `renox_agt_<64 hex>`, valid one hour, with no refresh token. Only its SHA-256 is stored (`auth__agent_tokens`).
- Revoking: the account page's "Connected agents" lists each live token with its client, scopes and last use. "Disconnect" revokes one and emits `auth.agent_token_revoked`, and the cell refuses the token from then on.

Proof: `tests/oauth.test.ts`:

- the full flow;
- a wrong verifier and a reused code;
- a narrowed scope;
- deny;
- no PKCE and an unregistered redirect;
- revoke from the account page;
- a consent page that cannot be framed and sets no cookie.

These keep the `docs/24-threat-model.md` row "Account takeover of a tenant developer" whole: agent tokens are hashed, last one hour, are listed, and can be revoked.

## Policies

`policies/auth.cedar` (a user reads and updates only their own account and revokes only their own sessions) and `policies/tests/auth.json` hold the default policy and its cases. They are files only until the policy engine (F5); `renox test` lists the cases as pending.

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs `tests/*.test.ts` in `tests/app/`, with the fixture modules `reader`, `mailer` and `otpbox`. `otpbox` records codes in place of whatsapp, extends the principal, and halts `auth.after_login` for chosen users. The tests cover:

- register, login, logout, rotation, expiry, buckets, the public view, magic links, reset;
- OAuth with a fake provider, and UAE PASS with a fake IdP;
- the principal: its shape, filler attributes, roles, logout;
- phone sign-in;
- passkeys with recorded vectors;
- agents (OAuth 2.1 for `/mcp`);
- install and upgrade into the shop;
- per-role snapshots (`tests/__snapshots__/`).

## Security tests

`tests/negative/` (#100): one file per attack, with the `docs/24-threat-model.md` F4 and `docs/23-failure-modes.md` section 5 rows each one proves.

| File | Case | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session-fixation.test.ts` | A session token planted in the victim's browser before sign-in | A new token at sign-in; the planted one is revoked |
| `session-fixation.test.ts` | Password change | This session rotated, every other one signed out |
| `logout.test.ts` | A cookie copied before logout, replayed after | Refused (server-side revocation); "sign out everywhere" ends every session |
| `token-replay.test.ts` | Magic link used twice; from another browser family | Refused; tokens live 15 minutes and are stored hashed |
| `token-replay.test.ts` | Reset token reused, or past 15 minutes | Refused; the password stays |
| `oauth-state-pkce.test.ts` | Callback with a forged state, another flow's state, or no flow cookie | Refused before the code exchange, no session |
| `oauth-state-pkce.test.ts` | Code exchanged with another PKCE verifier | Refused by the provider (a fake Google in the test process) |
| `enumeration.test.ts` | Login, register, reset, magic link for an existing and a missing account | The same status and message, no cookie at register; timing within 20 % |
| `brute-force.test.ts` | 10 failures per account, 30 per IP in 15 minutes | Locked with the generic message, which is snapshotted with the register, reset and magic-link messages; unlocked in the next window |
| `password-hashing.test.ts` | The stored hash | argon2id v19, m = 65536, t = 3, p = 1, 16-byte salt, 32-byte digest, a different salt per user |
| `cookies.test.ts` | The session, logout and OAuth flow cookies | `__Host-`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` |

## Language

auth's pages ask `i18n.detectLocale` for the locale, passing the signed-in user, and set it. Their text comes from `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/ar.json`, keys `auth.*`. An app re-words a label with the same key in its own catalog. Messages computed in code (errors, notices) are English for now.

---

Source: modules/billing/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/billing/README.md)

# billing (#329)

Payments for an app's own customers:
- plans and subscriptions;
- one-off checkouts, one per order;
- invoices, refunds and metered usage;
- a PSP adapter, with Stripe UAE first and the GCC providers in #330;
- Stripe's webhooks, verified by the platform.

Amounts are integers in minor units (fils for AED). Card data never reaches the app: the customer pays on the provider's page.

## Install

```sh
bunx renox add billing                                   # needs auth and i18n
bunx renox secrets set BILLING_STRIPE_KEY sk_live_…      # or sk_test_… while testing
bunx renox secrets set BILLING_WEBHOOK_STRIPE_SECRET whsec_…
```

```toml
billing = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/billing", config = { currency = "AED", success_url = "/orders", cancel_url = "/cart" } }
```

In the Stripe dashboard, point a webhook endpoint at `https://<app host>/billing/webhooks/stripe`. Send it these events:
- `checkout.session.completed`
- `invoice.finalized`
- `invoice.paid`
- `invoice.payment_failed`
- `payment_intent.payment_failed`
- `customer.subscription.deleted`
- `charge.refunded`
- `charge.dispute.created`

## Services

| Service | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `createPlan({ id, name, amount, interval })`, `plans()` | Define and list plans; `interval` is `month` or `year` |
| `createCheckout({ order_id, customer_id, plan_id })` or `({ order_id, customer_id, amount, description })` | A subscription, or a one-off payment. One checkout per `order_id`: asking again for an open session answers the same session (`reused: true`, no second charge); a paid order is `CONFLICT`. `billing.fraud_signal` runs first |
| `checkout(customer_id, plan_id)` | A subscription checkout whose order is the customer and the plan |
| `getSubscription(customer_id)`, `listInvoices(customer_id)` | Read a customer's state |
| `recordUsage(customer_id, metric, quantity)`, `usage(customer_id, metric, since)` | Metered usage |
| `refund(invoice_id, amount)` | Needs `billing.refund`. Never more than was paid less what was already refunded; the PSP call is idempotent |

Errors are `BillingError` with a code: `INVALID`, `NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `PSP`, `CONFLICT` or `REFUSED`.

## Events and hooks

| Name | Kind | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `billing.checkout_completed` | event | A checkout was paid |
| `billing.payment_received` | event | Money arrived for an invoice |
| `billing.payment_failed` | event | A payment failed; the subscription is now `past_due`. Dunning emails are the app's handler of this event (through `email.send`) |
| `billing.invoice_issued` | event | The PSP issued an invoice; tax-gcc numbers its tax invoice from this (#331) |
| `billing.invoice_paid`, `billing.subscription_changed`, `billing.refunded` | events | Self-explanatory |
| `billing.disputed` | event | A customer disputed a payment with their bank (`charge.dispute.created`): the invoice or one-off order of its payment intent, the amount and Stripe's reason. The invoice row keeps `disputed_at`; the evidence is answered in the Stripe dashboard |
| `billing.fraud_signal` | hook point | Receives `{ customer_id, order_id, amount, currency, mode }` before a checkout session is created. A halt refuses the checkout; the card-testing limits are #123 |

The public view `billing__public_user_plans_v1` (`user_id`, `plan_id`, `status`, `current_period_end`) is what other modules read a user's plan through.

## Pages and roles

| Page | Who | What it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<mount>` | Signed-in users | The plans, the user's subscription and invoices, and **Subscribe** |
| `<mount>/invoices` | Needs `billing.manage` | Every invoice |
| Refund form | Needs `billing.refund` (`r-can`) | Shown on the invoices page |

The default policy (`policies/billing.cedar`):
- `admin` holds both actions;
- `finance` holds `billing.manage` only.

`billing.refund` is sensitive, so every decision on it is audited.

## The adapter

`lib/adapter.ts` defines the adapter interface:
- `createSession`: Stripe's call carries the idempotency key `checkout:<order_id>`;
- `capture`;
- `refund`;
- `parseWebhook`, which normalises the provider's events.

#330 adds the GCC providers behind the same interface.

## Payment methods and adapters (#330)

`config.methods` lists the methods offered, from `card`, `cod` and `bank`; the default is `card`. `createCheckout({ …, method })` refuses a method the app did not enable. `cod` and `bank` are for one-off payments only.

| Method | Adapter | State | Go-live steps (owner) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Card, Stripe UAE | `lib/adapter.ts` `stripe` | Built and tested against recorded request shapes | Stripe account, keys, webhook endpoint (above) |
| Cash on delivery | `src/adapters/offline.ts` | Built. States: `placed` → `out_for_delivery` → `delivered` (paid) or `refused` (unpaid), moved with `codUpdate`, which needs `billing.manage` | None; the courier's confirmation is the app's own call |
| Bank transfer | `src/adapters/offline.ts` | Built. Each order gets a reference `RNX-XXXXXXXX`, shown with `bank_name`, `bank_beneficiary` and `bank_iban` on `<mount>/checkout/pending`. `<mount>/checkout/import` takes the statement as CSV, and `matchTransfer` pays an order only when the reference and the exact amount match. Anything else stays unmatched for a person to check | Fill the bank config; export statements as CSV with `date`, `amount` and `description` columns |
| Checkout.com, Telr, PayTabs, N-Genius | — | **Not built** (#330 stays open): no adapter is written before it can be checked against the provider's sandbox | A merchant account, sandbox credentials, and the webhook secret `BILLING_WEBHOOK_<PROVIDER>_SECRET` per provider |
| Apple Pay and Google Pay | — | **Not built**: they come as payment methods of the card PSPs above | Apple's domain verification file served from the app; Google Pay merchant id |
| Tabby, Tamara (BNPL) | — | **Not built**, including the eligibility rules (amount range, currency) and the rejected path | Merchant account and sandbox with each |

## Owner steps

- A Stripe account, and the live and test keys.
- The webhook endpoint and its signing secret.
- 3DS left on, which is Stripe's default.

## Tests

- `bun test` runs the unit tests on SQLite, with the PSP replaced by a recording stand-in:
  - the Stripe requests, from recorded fixtures;
  - one checkout per order, and the double click;
  - `billing.fraud_signal`;
  - refunds and their limits;
  - every webhook path.
- With `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`, `tests/app.test.ts` runs in an app on the worker:
  - a bad signature gets 401, and a replay is answered `duplicate`;
  - the customer's page;
  - the invoices page per role (none, finance, admin).
- `examples/shop` has the module installed.

Source: modules/booking/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/booking/README.md)

# booking (#334)

Appointments for salons, clinics and other services:
- **Services and staff**, with weekly and dated hours (Ramadan hours, holidays). Slots are computed in the app's time zone; the UAE has no DST.
- **Holds** that expire.
- **Deposits** paid through `billing`.
- **Cancellation** with a window, and no-shows.
- **Reminders** 24 h and 2 h before, through `email`.
- **A staff calendar** that updates live over the change feed.

## Install

```sh
bunx renox add booking          # needs auth, i18n, billing and email
```

```toml
booking = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/booking", config = { slot_minutes = 15, hold_minutes = 10 } }
```

To set up the catalogue, an admin's app code calls:
- `booking.addService({ id, name, minutes, buffer?, deposit_fils?, cancel_hours? })`
- `booking.addStaff({ id, name, user_id, services })`
- `booking.setHours(staff, weekday | "YYYY-MM-DD", open_min, close_min)`

All three need `booking.manage`.

## Services and events

| Service | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `slots(service, day, { staff? })` | The free starts of a day: weekly and dated hours, the service's length and buffer, live bookings, and holds not yet expired |
| `hold(service, staff, start, customer)` (also `book`) | Holds the slot. With a deposit it answers `pay_url`, the billing checkout of order `booking:<id>`; paying it confirms the booking. Otherwise `confirm` follows. A taken slot is `TAKEN` |
| `confirm(id)` | Confirms the booking, emits `booking.confirmed`, and queues the reminders |
| `cancel(id)` | Inside the service's `cancel_hours` before the start, a paid deposit is retained. `booking.cancelled` says which; the refund itself is `billing.refund` |
| `noShow(id)` | Marks a confirmed booking whose start has passed |

**No double booking.** The slot search refuses a taken start. A unique index allows one live booking per staff member and start, so the second writer of a race is answered "taken".

**Reminders.** `jobs/reminder.ts` runs are queued at confirmation for 24 h and 2 h before the start. Each kind is sent once (`booking__reminders`), and only while the booking is still confirmed. They go by email to the customer's address in auth's public view. WhatsApp templates are not wired; they are the `whatsapp` module's.

## Pages and roles

| Page | Who | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<mount>?service=&day=` | Signed-in customers | The services, then a day's free slots; a slot holds and confirms, or goes to the deposit checkout |
| `<mount>/mine` | The customer | Their own bookings only, with cancel |
| `<mount>/calendar` | `booking.view_calendar` | The staff member's day |

The calendar's `<mount>/sse/calendar` subscribes the staff member to `calendar:<their staff id>`. `[realtime.feeds]` publishes each committed change of `booking__bookings` there.

Default policy:
- `admin` has `booking.manage` and `booking.view_calendar`;
- `staff` has `booking.view_calendar` and may subscribe to `calendar:*`.

## Not built

- WhatsApp reminders.
- The `org` scope for several branches.
- Classes with capacity.

## Tests

- `bun test` runs the unit tests:
  - slots from weekly and Ramadan hours, buffers, holds that expire;
  - the live-booking index;
  - a deposit confirming the booking and queueing both reminders, each sent once;
  - cancellation inside and outside the window, a reminder after a cancel not sent, and no-shows.
- With `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`, `tests/app.test.ts` runs in an app with billing and email on the worker:
  - a customer books through the page;
  - each customer sees only their own bookings;
  - both reminders are queued at 24 h and 2 h before;
  - two customers racing for one slot get one booking;
  - the calendar is refused without the role;
  - the staff member's open stream receives the next booking.

Source: modules/email/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/email/README.md)

# email (#328)

Transactional email for apps and modules.
- Templates in English and Arabic, side by side in one message.
- Sent through **Resend** or **Amazon SES**, queued through the outbox with retries.
- A suppression list fed by bounces and complaints.
- A message log page for admins.

Bodies are never logged.

## Install

```sh
bunx renox add email          # needs auth and i18n
bunx renox secrets set EMAIL_RESEND_KEY re_…                       # provider = resend
bunx renox secrets set EMAIL_SES_ACCESS_KEY …; bunx renox secrets set EMAIL_SES_SECRET_KEY …   # provider = ses
bunx renox secrets set EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET …                      # the bounce and complaint relay
```

`renox.toml`:

```toml
email = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/email", config = { provider = "resend", from = "orders@yourshop.ae" } }
```

## Config

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `resend` | `resend` or `ses` |
| `from` | (empty) | The From address, on a domain verified with the provider. Until it is set, nothing is sent and messages end as `failed` with `not_configured` |
| `ses_region` | `me-central-1` | The SES region |
| `sends_per_minute` | 120 | Past it, `send` refuses (`RATE_LIMITED`) |
| `base_path` | `/email` | Where the log page is mounted |

## Services

| Service | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `send(to, template, data, { locale?, reply_to? })` | Queues one of the templates below in the recipient's locale (`en` or `ar`); the other language follows in the same message. Answers `{ id }`, or `{ id: null, cancelled: true }` when `email.before_send` halts. A suppressed address is refused with `SUPPRESSED` |
| `sendRaw({ to, subject, text?, html?, reply_to? })` | Queues a message the caller wrote itself |
| `status(id)` | `{ status, attempts, error }`, where status is `queued`, `sent`, `failed` or `suppressed` |
| `suppress(address, reason)`, `unsuppress(address)`, `isSuppressed(address)` | Manage the suppression list |

**Templates** (`lib/templates.ts`): `verify_email`, `password_reset`, `magic_link`, `account_exists`, `welcome`.
- The values are `display_name`, `url` (only `https`, or `http` on localhost) and `expires_minutes`.
- Every value is escaped, and the HTML is a two-column table: one column `lang="en" dir="ltr"`, the other `lang="ar" dir="rtl"`.
- A different wording means a new template here.

## Adapters

| Provider | How it sends | Retries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resend | `POST https://api.resend.com/emails` with `EMAIL_RESEND_KEY` | A 5xx, a 429 or a network failure throws, so the outbox retries with backoff and dead-letters after its last attempt. A 4xx is final (`failed`) |
| SES v2 | `POST https://email.<region>.amazonaws.com/v2/email/outbound-emails`, signed with SigV4 using `EMAIL_SES_ACCESS_KEY` and `EMAIL_SES_SECRET_KEY` | Same as Resend |
| SMTP | Not available: an isolate has no raw sockets. Use a provider's HTTP API, or an HTTP relay in front of SMTP | — |

## Events and hooks

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email.send_requested` | event (own) | A message was queued; the module's handler sends it after the commit |
| `email.bounced`, `email.complained` | events | `{ address }`: the address is now suppressed |
| `email.before_send` | hook point | `{ template, locale, to_domain }`, never the body: a filler that halts stops the message (the app's own sending policy) |
| `auth.send_mail` | hook filled | auth's confirmation, reset, magic-link and account-exists emails, from the templates |
| `auth.user_registered` | event handled | The `welcome` email, to the address in `auth__public_users_v1` |
| `notifications.deliver` | hook filled | The `email` channel of the notifications module |

## Feedback

The provider's bounce and complaint notifications are relayed to `POST <mount>/webhooks/feedback`, checked with the generic HMAC scheme of `webhook.verify` and `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

Resend's own scheme (Svix) and SES's (SNS) are not in the `webhook.verify` contract (`ops.md` 1.7.0 section 22), so they need a relay that re-signs, until a contract version adds them.

## The log page

`<mount>` (`/email`) needs `email.read_log`. It lists the latest 100 messages (recipient, subject, template, state, attempts) and the suppressed addresses, never a body. **Allow again** needs `email.manage`.

The default policy (`policies/email.cedar`) grants both actions to the `admin` role, which the app assigns. `email.manage` is sensitive, so every decision on it is audited.

## Owner steps

- Verify the sending domain with the provider: DKIM, SPF, and a DMARC record. Set `from` to an address on that domain.
- Create the provider key (Resend, or an SES IAM user with `ses:SendEmail` only) and set the secrets above.
- Point the provider's bounce and complaint notifications at the relay that signs for `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

## Tests

- `bun test` in this directory runs the unit tests on SQLite:
  - each adapter's request against a fake;
  - suppression, retries, the bounce path;
  - the bilingual snapshots in `ltr` and `rtl`;
  - `email.before_send`, `reply_to`, and the `auth.send_mail` filler.
- With `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`, `tests/app.test.ts` runs in an app on the worker. It checks the confirmation and welcome emails of a registration, and the log page refused without the role and shown to an admin with no body.
- `examples/shop/tests/email.test.ts` installs the module on the shop.

Source: modules/gcc/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/gcc/README.md)

# gcc

UAE data and checks for any app or module (catalog label "gcc-data"; `docs/21-uae-gcc-strategy.md` row M23):

- the seven emirates and their areas;
- +971 phone numbers;
- Emirates ID (with its check digit), TRN, trade licence numbers, Makani numbers and P.O. Boxes;
- an address partial and a phone partial in English and Arabic.

It has no dependencies, no network, and no secrets.

## Install

```sh
renox add gcc
```

```toml
[modules]
gcc = { version = "^1.0" }          # mounted at /gcc: the area lookup is /gcc/areas
```

## Services

Through `import { gcc } from "renox:modules"`. Each validator answers `{ ok: true, value }` (the normalised form) or `{ ok: false, reason }`.

| Service | Checks | `value` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `validatePhone(s)` | Mobile `5[024568]` + 7 digits, landline `[2-4679]` + 7 digits; accepts `+971`, `00971`, `971`, `0`, spaces, dashes, brackets | E.164, `+971501234567` |
| `validateEmiratesId(s)` | 15 digits, `784`, a year 1900–2100, the Luhn check digit | `784-1990-1234567-6` |
| `validateTrn(s)` | 15 digits (format only: the FTA register is not consulted) | the digits |
| `validateTradeLicence(s, emirate)` | The shape for the issuing emirate: Abu Dhabi `CN-` + 6–8 digits, Dubai 6–8 digits, Sharjah 5–8, Ajman 4–8, the others 4–20 letters, digits and dashes (format only) | upper case |
| `validateMakani(s)` | 10 digits | the digits |
| `validatePoBox(s)` | 1–6 digits, with or without "P.O. Box" | the digits |
| `listAreas(emirate)` | Areas of an emirate (`AE-AZ`, `AE-DU`, `AE-SH`, `AE-AJ`, `AE-UQ`, `AE-RK`, `AE-FU`, ISO 3166-2:AE), by English name | |
| `findAreas(q, emirate?)` | Areas whose English or Arabic name starts with `q`, at most 20, one indexed query | |

The same checks are pure functions in `lib/validators.ts`, with no I/O. Code that runs outside the isolate (a browser bundle, a script) imports that file directly.

## Partials

- `<gcc:address emirate area po_box makani areas_url>`: an emirate select, an area field that asks `/gcc/areas` for the `area_list` fragment as you type (htmx), a P.O. Box, and a Makani number.
- `<gcc:phone name value>`: a `tel` input that holds the E.164 value (`dir="ltr"`), with the number formatted for reading next to it by the platform's `phone_ae` filter. In Arabic the formatted text is wrapped in LTR isolates, which belong in text, never in an input value.

Labels come from `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/ar.json`, keys `gcc.*`. An app overrides a label with the same key in its own catalog.

## Tables and views

`gcc__areas` (`emirate`, `name_en`, `name_ar`, `makani`: 1 for Dubai, where Makani numbers are the address). Other modules read it through `gcc__public_areas_v1`.

## Data

The seed (`migrations/002_seed_areas.sql`, as of 2026-10-29) is a starter list of well-known areas per emirate, names in English and Arabic, written for this module. It is not an official registry, and it is not complete. For a full list, use the emirates' official address data (Dubai Municipality's community list and Makani, the Abu Dhabi and Sharjah municipalities). Areas are added by a later version of this module (a new migration): an app cannot write `gcc__` tables.

## Permissions

| What | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Tables | `gcc__*` |
| Network, secrets, slots, hooks | none |

Policy: `gcc.read` is public (`policies/gcc.cedar`; files only until F5).

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs:

- `tests/validators.test.ts`: plain Bun, every branch, 100 % of the lines and functions of `lib/validators.ts` with `--coverage`;
- `tests/gcc.test.ts`: on the worker. The services through the broker; the `Dub` fragment (4 areas, one indexed query, median under 10 ms on the dev container); the partials in English and Arabic, snapshotted.

Source: modules/i18n/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/i18n/README.md)

# i18n

Chooses the locale of each page and keeps each user's choice. Ships the right-to-left CSS baseline. The official modules (`auth`, `org`, `gcc`) ship English and Arabic catalogs that work with it (`docs/08-template-engine.md`, RTL; `docs/21-uae-gcc-strategy.md`).

It has no dependencies, no network, and no secrets.

## Install

```sh
renox add i18n
```

```toml
[modules]
i18n = { version = "^1.0", config = { locales = "en,ar", default_locale = "en" } }
```

| Config | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `locales` | `en,ar` | The locales the app offers, comma separated |
| `default_locale` | `en` | Used when nothing else decides |
| `digits` | `latn` | Digits on Arabic pages: `latn`, `arab` (Eastern Arabic), or `auto`, which follows the stored choice (below) |
| `calendar` | `gregory` | Calendar on Arabic pages: `gregory`, `islamic-umalqura` (Hijri), or `auto`, which follows the stored choice ("Hijri dates", below) |

`auth` and `org` depend on i18n. Installing either installs nothing implicitly, so add i18n first.

## Choosing the locale

`detectLocale({ user_id?, org_locale? })` takes the first offered locale from this list:

1. `?lang=` in the URL. It is stored for the user, or for the page session when there is no user.
2. The user's stored choice.
3. The page session's stored choice.
4. The organisation's default (`org_locale`).
5. `Accept-Language`, by quality.
6. `default_locale`.

A candidate counts only when it is offered (`ar-AE` matches `ar`). The result is `{ locale, dir, digits, calendar, source, alternates }`. `alternates` has one link per offered locale: this page with `?lang=`.

i18n never sets the page locale itself (`ops.md` 1.3.0 section 14, "Locale"). The loader does:

```ts
import { auth, i18n, org } from "renox:modules";

export async function load(ctx) {
  const user = await auth.currentUser();
  const current = await org.currentOrg();
  const r = await i18n.detectLocale({ user_id: user?.id ?? null, org_locale: current?.locale ?? null });
  ctx.setLocale(r.locale, r.dir);
  return { i18n_links: r.alternates /* , ... */ };
}
```

i18n takes the user and the organisation default as arguments; it does not look them up itself. `auth` and `org` call i18n from their own pages, so i18n cannot depend on them: the dependency graph has no cycles (`docs/10-modules.md`, rule 1), and a manifest has no optional dependencies.

`setLocale(locale, { user_id? })` stores a choice without a `?lang=` link, for example from an account page.

The hook `i18n.detect` runs before the choice. A module may fill it and halt with its own response, such as a redirect to a canonical address. Apps cannot fill hooks (`docs/contracts/manifest.md`).

## Language links

```html
<i18n:language :links="i18n_links" />
```

The partial renders the current locale as text and the others as links to this page with `?lang=`.

## Catalogs

Each module ships `i18n/<locale>.json`. Nested objects are flattened to dotted keys, and messages use the ICU subset of `docs/08-template-engine.md`. Use `<r-t key="…" />`, or the `t` filter in an attribute: `:placeholder="'shop.list.search' | t"`.

- **A module's keys** start with the module's name (`auth.login.title`).
- **The app's catalogs** go in `i18n/<locale>.json` at the app's root. They override any module's key, so an app re-words a module without overriding a template.
- **Adding a locale** to an app:
  1. Add it to `locales`.
  2. Add `i18n/<locale>.json` with the keys of your templates.
  3. Add the official modules' keys you want translated; missing keys fall back to English.
- **Machine translation:** a catalog that was machine translated says so under `_meta`. The Arabic catalogs of `auth`, `org`, `shop` and this module are, until a native speaker reviews them (an owner task).

## Completeness and the glossary (#336)

`renox check` reports `i18n-missing-key` (an error) in two cases:
- a key that one of the app's or a module's `i18n/<locale>.json` catalogs has and another does not;
- a `<r-t key>` in a template that a declared locale does not translate.

`_meta` (a catalog's review status) is not text and is not compared. `cli/tests/lint.test.ts` runs the rule over every module, the examples, the dashboard and `www/`.

The Arabic terms the modules share are in [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md).

## RTL snapshots (#336)

Every page of every official module is rendered in `en` (`<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`) and `ar` (`<html lang="ar" dir="rtl">`) by the module's `tests/rtl.test.ts`, and both are snapshotted under `tests/__snapshots__/`. The shared helper `tests/rtl.ts` (`bothDirections`) also fails a page whose Arabic render still shows the English message of one of its keys (from its template or the module's layouts), or a key rendered as itself.

## RTL baseline

`public/i18n.css` uses logical properties (`margin-inline`, `padding-inline`, `text-align: start`). It keeps numbers, phone numbers, emails and codes left to right inside Arabic text, and places htmx indicators after their control. Modules cannot serve public files yet (artifact 1.1), so copy it into the app's `public/`. The shop's own fixes are in `examples/shop/public/app.css`.

## Arabic digits

An Arabic page gets Eastern Arabic digits (`١٢٣٫٤٥`, `١٬٢٣٤٫٥٠ د.إ.`) in the `number`, `money` and `date` filters when its tag carries `-u-nu-arab` (`ops.md` 1.4.0, "Locale"). `detectLocale` builds that tag from `digits`:

- `latn`: never; `ar`.
- `arab`: always on Arabic pages; `ar-u-nu-arab`.
- `auto`: when the choice that won asked for it. `?lang=ar-u-nu-arab` (or `setLocale("ar-u-nu-arab", …)`) stores `digits = 'arab'` with the choice, and `?lang=ar` or `ar-u-nu-latn` stores Latin.

The loader passes the returned `locale` to `ctx.setLocale` unchanged. `<html lang>` then carries the full tag, and catalogs are looked up by the language (`ar`). Only `nu-arab` is rendered. `arabext` (Persian digits) is accepted by the contract but renders Latin digits until the renderer supports it.

## Hijri dates

`calendar` builds the `ca` key of the same `-u-` extension: `?lang=ar-u-ca-islamic-umalqura` (with `auto`) stores `calendar = 'islamic-umalqura'` with the choice, and the page tag becomes `ar-u-ca-islamic-umalqura`, or `ar-u-ca-islamic-umalqura-nu-arab` with Eastern Arabic digits (`ca` before `nu`, as `ops.md` 1.4.0 requires). English pages stay Gregorian. `detectLocale` returns it as `calendar`.

The renderer's `date` filter formats the Gregorian calendar only, so a page that shows a Hijri date formats it in its loader with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(tag)` and shows it next to the Gregorian one: the booking pages and the tax invoice do (`lib/hijri.ts` of each).

## Mirrored icons

An icon that points (an arrow, a chevron) carries `class="i18n-mirror"`; `public/i18n.css` flips it on `dir="rtl"` pages. The booking calendar's day arrows use it.

## Tables

`i18n__prefs`: `subject` (`user:<id>` or `session:<page session id>`), `locale`, `digits` (`arab`, `latn` or null, migration 002), `calendar` (a calendar of `ops.md` 1.4.0 or null, migration 003), `updated_at`.

---

Source: modules/jobs/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/jobs/README.md)

# jobs

The app's scheduled and queued jobs as a page (#297; `docs/contracts/ops.md` 1.6.0 section 20, `docs/18-build-plan.md` M10). The platform keeps the runs: a job file exports `schedule` and `run`, the cell's scheduler writes one durable run per tick, the outbox worker runs it with retries and dead letters. This module only shows them and lets an admin retry or cancel a run.

## Install

```toml
[modules]
jobs = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/jobs" }
```

It needs `auth` (the login hop) and `i18n` (EN and AR).

## Page

`GET /jobs` (the mount): four lists.

| List | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Scheduled | Every `job` route of the active deployment, its next tick and when it last finished |
| Queued | Runs waiting for their time or a retry, with their attempts |
| Running | Runs in flight and when they started |
| Failed (dead letters) | Runs that used all their attempts, with the redacted last error (an error code or `threw`, at most 512 characters) |

A payload is never shown or returned. `POST ?/retry` puts a dead run back in the queue with its attempts reset; `POST ?/cancel` deletes a queued or dead run (a running run is refused until it ends; a scheduled job is not cancelled: it follows its `schedule`).

## Permissions

| Action | Default role | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jobs.read` | `admin`, `operator` | The page and `list` |
| `jobs.manage` | `admin` | `retry` and `cancel`; sensitive, so every decision is a row of `renox__authz_audit`, besides the op's own row (`jobs.retry`, `jobs.cancel`) |

The app grants the roles (`ctx.authz.roles.assign(user, "admin")`); the module never grants them. The page has `guard = { action: "jobs.read" }`: a user without it gets 403.

## Services

| Service | What |
| --- | --- |
| `list(state, { limit?, cursor? })` | `{ items, next_cursor }` of `scheduled`, `queued`, `running` or `dead` (`JobRow`: `id`, `name`, `module`, `tick`, `next_at`, `run_at`, `attempts`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `last_error`) |
| `retry(id)` | A dead run back in the queue |
| `cancel(id)` | A queued or dead run deleted |

Each checks the app's policy first, then calls `ctx.jobs.list`, `retry` or `cancel`: the platform answers those ops only to this module (`RENOX_FORBIDDEN` for the app and any other module). Errors: `RENOX_JOB_NOT_FOUND`, `RENOX_JOB_STATE` (retry of a run that is not dead, cancel of a running run).

## Config

| Key | Default | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `base_path` | `/jobs` | Where the app mounts the pages |

## Writing a job

```ts
// jobs/nightly-report.ts (the app) or modules/<name>/jobs/<name>.ts (a module)
export const schedule = "0 3 * * *";   // minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week
export const tz = "Asia/Dubai";         // optional; UTC when absent
export async function run(ctx) {
  // ctx.job: { id, name, tick, attempt, payload }; ctx.db is this attempt's transaction
}
```

`ctx.jobs.enqueue("nightly-report", { day: "2026-10-30" }, { runAt })` queues a run of one of the caller's own jobs, in the current transaction. Under `renox dev`, scheduled jobs run with `--jobs`, and `renox jobs list|run|retry` works on the dev database.

## Tests

`tests/jobs.test.ts` through `renox test` (or `bun test` with `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`): the four lists without a payload (snapshot of the failed list), retry and cancel with their audit rows, an operator reading but not retrying, a user without a role and the app's own broker call refused. `policies/tests/jobs.json`: the default policies per role.

---

Source: modules/notifications/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/notifications/README.md)

# notifications

In-app notifications (`docs/18-build-plan.md` M9). A module or the app calls `notify(user, item)`. The user's open pages update their badge and list without a reload, over SSE (`docs/09-htmx-realtime.md`). The user chooses per category which channels they get.

## Install

```toml
[modules]
notifications = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/notifications", config = { channels = "whatsapp" } }
```

It needs `auth` (the signed-in user, the login hop) and `i18n` (the page language).

| Config | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `base_path` | `/notifications` | Where the app mounts the module, for the badge's links |
| `channels` | `""` | Other channels, comma-separated (`whatsapp`, `email`). The module runs `notifications.deliver` for each one the user has not turned off |

## Service

```ts
import { notifications } from "renox:modules";

await notifications.notify(userId, { category: "orders", title: "Order #42 shipped", body: "On its way", link: "/orders/42" });
```

| Service | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `notify(user, { category, title, body?, link? })` | `{ id, channels }`. It writes the row and pushes the badge and the item to `notif:user:<user>`. Then it runs `notifications.deliver` once for each other channel. Every channel, in-app included, honours the user's preferences. `id` is `null` when the user turned in-app off for the category. The arguments must be: `category` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]*`; `title` from 1 to 200 characters; `body` up to 2000 characters. `link` is kept only when it is a path of the app or an `https` URL |
| `list({ unread?, limit? })` | The signed-in user's notifications, newest first (at most 100) |
| `unreadCount()` | The signed-in user's unread count |
| `markRead(id)`, `markAllRead()` | Marks one notification (or all of them) read, and pushes the new count |
| `preferences()`, `setPreference({ category, channel, enabled })` | The signed-in user's channels per category: `inapp` plus the configured ones. Everything is on until turned off |
| `badge()` | The header badge's data, or `null` when signed out |

`notifications__items` and `notifications__prefs` are owned by `user_id` (`[authz.ownership]`). Every statement goes through `db.scoped()`, so one user's call never reads or changes another user's rows.

## Hook

`notifications.deliver` receives `{ user, channel, item: { id, category, title, body, link } }` once per enabled channel. `whatsapp` (#290) fills it for `whatsapp`, and `email` will fill it in F7. A filler declares it with `permissions.hooks = ["notifications.deliver"]`.

## Slot

`partials/badge.html` fills `app.header`: a link to the list with the unread count, which updates live (`hx-ext="sse"`, `sse-swap="notif-badge"`). The host page puts the badge's data in its own data:

```ts
import { notifications } from "renox:modules";

export async function load() {
  return { notif_badge: await notifications.badge() };
}
```

## Pages and the live stream

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET <mount>` | The list, live: new items at the top (`sse-swap="notif-item"`). Actions `read` and `all` |
| `GET <mount>/prefs` | Channels per category. Action `set` |
| `GET <mount>/sse/notifications` | The SSE stream of the signed-in user. It subscribes the connection to `notif:user:<principal id>`. Events: `notif-badge` (`partials/count.html`) and `notif-item` (`partials/item.html`) |

Signed out, the pages send the visitor to auth's login page, and the stream ends at once.

## Policy

Subscribing is the platform action `realtime.subscribe`, and it is fail-closed. `policies/notifications.cedar` allows a user only their own topic:

```cedar
permit (principal is Renox::User, action == Renox::Action::"realtime.subscribe", resource is Renox::Topic)
when { resource.name like "notif:user:*" && resource.segments.contains(principal.id) };
```

User ids are auth's 32 hex digits, so no id can equal the segments `notif` or `user`.

## Listeners

`org.member_added` for a member who is not the owner: "You joined an organisation". auth has no "login from a new device" event yet, so there is no listener for it. Apps add their own notifications through `notify`.

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs `tests/notifications.test.ts` against `tests/app`. That app has auth, org, notifications, and `deliver`, a fixture that records `notifications.deliver`. The tests cover:

- two SSE clients: a notification reaches alice's badge and list, never bob's;
- bob's subscribe to alice's topic through another route is refused (`docs/24-threat-model.md` "Subscribing to another user's topic");
- a signed-out stream gets nothing;
- the header badge, the unread count, and mark read with the badge following live;
- a preference stopping WhatsApp, then in-app;
- links;
- snapshots in English and Arabic.

---

Source: modules/org/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/org/README.md)

# org

Organisations for any app (`docs/18-build-plan.md` M2): a user belongs to one or more organisations with a role, invites others by email, and switches the active organisation. The app gets the active organisation and the user's role from one service call, with no org code of its own.

It depends on `auth ^1.0` (users and sessions) and `i18n ^1.0` (the page locale). It has no network and no secrets.

## Install

```sh
renox add i18n
renox add auth
renox add org
```

```toml
[modules]
auth = { version = "^1.0" }
org = { version = "^1.0" }   # mounted at /org
```

| Config | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `base_path` | `/org` | Where the app mounts org's pages; the switcher posts there. Set it when you change the mount |
| `invite_days` | `7` | An invitation expires this many days after it was sent |

## Roles

`member` < `admin` < `owner`.

- Every member reads the members list and may leave.
- An admin also invites, withdraws invitations, changes roles, and removes members. An admin never changes or removes an owner, and never grants `owner`.
- An owner does all of that for every member, owners included.
- The last owner of an organisation cannot be removed, leave, or be demoted. Make someone else owner first.

## Services

Through `import { org } from "renox:modules"`. A call the signed-in user's membership does not allow throws, and the caller sees `RENOX_MODULE_SERVICE`.

| Service | |
| --- | --- |
| `createOrg({ name, slug? })` | A new organisation. The signed-in user becomes its owner and it becomes the active one. `slug` defaults to the name in lower case with dashes, and it is unique. Returns `{ org }` or `{ error }` |
| `listOrgs(user_id)` | The user's organisations, each `{ id, slug, name, role }` |
| `currentOrg()` | The active organisation of this session, `{ id, slug, name, role, scope }`, or `null` |
| `requireMember(role?)` | The active organisation, or throws when the user is signed out or holds less than `role` |
| `switchOrg(org_id)` | Make another of the user's organisations active |
| `members(org_id)` | `[{ user_id, display_name, email, role }]`. The caller must be a member of that organisation |
| `invite({ org, email, role })` | Admin or owner. The link goes out through `org.send_mail`. Returns `{ invite_id, expires_at }` or `{ error }` |
| `revokeInvite({ org, invite })` | Withdraw a pending invitation |
| `acceptInvite(token)` | Join as the signed-in user. The invitation works once, before it expires, and only for the email it was sent to |
| `setRole({ org, user, role })`, `removeMember({ org, user })` | See the roles above. `removeMember` with your own id means leaving |
| `switcher(next?)` | The data of the switcher partial, for a page's `load` |

`scope` is `{ org_id, role }`, the organisation part of the authz context of F5 (`docs/11-authorization.md`, `policies/org.cedar`).

**The fence between organisations is in these services.** The SQLite authorizer keeps other modules out of `org__*` tables, but it does not tell one organisation's rows from another's. Until F5 brings `db.scoped`, scope your own tables yourself: store `currentOrg().id` with a row and filter on it. The `shop` example does this for its orders.

## Active organisation

The active organisation is kept per auth session. It is stored in `org__active`, keyed by the session id from `auth.currentSession()`, so it ends when the session ends. Without a choice, or after the user leaves the chosen organisation, the active one is the first organisation the user joined.

## Language

Each organisation may have a default locale (`org__orgs.locale`), set by an admin or owner on the members page or with `setOrgLocale({ org, locale })`. org's pages pass it to `i18n.detectLocale` with the user. A member's own choice (`?lang=`) wins over it. The labels come from `i18n/en.json` and `i18n/ar.json`, keys `org.*`.

## Pages

| Path | |
| --- | --- |
| `/org` | Your organisations, switch, create one. `?/switch` takes `org` and `next`, then redirects to `next` (a path of the app only) |
| `/org/members` | The active organisation's members. Admins and owners also see invitations and manage members |
| `/org/accept/<token>` | The invitation link. A signed-out visitor goes through auth's login and comes back |

## The switcher

org fills the `app.header` slot with `partials/switcher.html`. The partial renders what the page's `load` returns as `org_switcher`:

```ts
import { auth, org } from "renox:modules";

export async function load({ url }) {
  return { auth_user: await auth.currentUser(), org_switcher: await org.switcher(url.pathname) };
}
```

A member sees a select of their organisations, labelled with their role in each. Admins and owners also get a link to the members page. A signed-in user with no organisation gets a link to create one. A signed-out visitor sees nothing.

`admin.sidebar` is reserved for the `admin` module (M5). org fills it with a link to the members page, shown only with `org.manage_members`.

## Events and hooks

| | Payload | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `org.created` | `{ org_id, user_id, at }` | event |
| `org.member_added` | `{ org_id, user_id, role, at }` | event: at creation (the owner) and on every accepted invitation |
| `org.member_removed` | `{ org_id, user_id, by, at }` | event |
| `org.before_invite` | `{ org_id, email, role, invited_by }` | hook: a filler may halt (seat limits, a domain allowlist). Its response is the answer and no invitation is created |
| `org.send_mail` | `{ to, template: "org_invite", args: { url, org_name, role, expires_days, invited_by } }` | hook: fill it to deliver invitations until the email module (F7) |

## App MCP tool

`invite_member` (`tools/invite-member.ts`, `[[tools]]` in `module.toml`) lets a user's agent invite someone to one of the user's organisations through the app's `/mcp`.

- The agent runs as the user. The Cedar action is `org.invite`, and the org services still require an admin or owner.
- The input is `{ org, email, role? }`.
- `confirm = true`: the first call is a preview, rolled back, that returns a confirmation token. The agent repeats the call with that token to send the invitation.

`tests/tools.test.ts` drives it end to end with an agent token from auth's OAuth flow.

## Tables and views

- `org__orgs`
- `org__members`, unique per organisation and user
- `org__invites`, which stores only the SHA-256 of the token
- `org__active`

Other modules read memberships through `org__public_members_v1` (`org_id`, `user_id`, `role`).

## Tests

`renox test` in this folder runs `tests/` against `tests/app`, which has auth, org, and a fixture that records mail and events. The tests cover:

- the fence between organisations;
- invitations: single use, expiry, withdrawal, the invited email, and the hook;
- the last owner;
- the events;
- the `invite_member` tool through `/mcp` (`tests/tools.test.ts`);
- snapshots of the switcher and the members page for an owner, an admin, a member and a non-member;
- install and upgrade into the shop.

---

Source: modules/reports/README.md (https://github.com/arif-rachim/renox.rs/blob/main/modules/reports/README.md)

# reports (#333)

Reports for an app:
- **Sales per day**, from `tax_gcc`'s tax invoices and credit notes.
- **Cash per day**, from `billing`'s payment and refund events.
- **A page** with a period filter.
- **Exports:** CSV, Excel `.xlsx` (written in TypeScript, no dependency), and the invoice import files of Xero, QuickBooks Online and Zoho Books.
- **A nightly summary**, kept as a snapshot and emailed.

## Install

```sh
bunx renox add reports          # needs tax_gcc, email, auth and i18n
```

```toml
reports = { version = "^1.0", mount = "/reports", config = { email_to = "accounts@yourshop.ae" } }
```

## Pages and roles

| Page or action | Needs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<mount>?from=&to=` | `reports.view` | Daily sales (documents, net, VAT, total) and cash (received, refunded, net) for the period |
| **Export** form | `reports.export` (`r-can`) | Downloads `sales` or `cash` as CSV or `.xlsx`, or an accounting import file |

The default policy grants both actions to `admin` and `finance`. `reports.export` is sensitive, so every export is an audit row: a file carries customers and amounts out of the app.

## Importing into an accounting product

Each import file has one row per invoice line. Credit notes are negative quantities, amounts are in AED, and the UAE tax code is chosen by the line's rate.

| Product | Export `kind` | Tax codes used | Import steps (owner) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Xero | `xero` | Standard Rated Income (5%), Zero Rated Income, Exempt Income | Business → Invoices → Import. Map account code `200` (Sales) to your own if it differs. The tax rates must exist under these names (Xero's UAE defaults) |
| QuickBooks Online | `quickbooks` | `SR 5%`, `ZR`, `EX` | Settings → Import data → Invoices. Turn on custom transaction numbers so the `INV-` numbers are kept. Check the tax codes match your UAE VAT agency setup |
| Zoho Books | `zoho` | VAT 5%, Zero Rate, Exempt | Sales → Invoices → Import. Choose "Invoice Number" for duplicate handling, so a re-import does not double an invoice |

The CSV has a UTF-8 BOM, so Excel opens Arabic text correctly. A cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is prefixed so it is never run as a formula. The `.xlsx` writes strings as inline text, never as formulas.

## The nightly report

`jobs/nightly.ts` runs at 03:00 UTC. It does the same as the `nightly(now_ms)` service, which can also be called directly:
- keeps yesterday's sales and cash totals in `reports__snapshots`;
- when `email_to` is set, sends them as CSV through `email.sendRaw`.

## Not built

- The bilingual PDF summary.
- Direct API pushes to the accounting products.
- A custom report builder.

## Tests

- `bun test` runs the unit tests:
  - daily sales with credit notes netted;
  - the CSV's BOM, quoting, Arabic and formula guard;
  - each accounting layout;
  - an `.xlsx` opened by the reader, with its CRCs checked, numbers as numbers and text as text;
  - the cash ledger counting a redelivered event once.
- With `RENOX_WORKER_PATH`, `tests/app.test.ts` runs in an app with billing, tax_gcc and email on the worker:
  - a PSP invoice issued and paid shows as the day's sales and cash;
  - the page is refused without `reports.view`;
  - the Excel export works;
  - the nightly report is kept as a snapshot and emailed.
